paper.title_en: Intertwined Magneto-Structural Criticality Driving Heterogeneous Collective-Pseudospin Dynamics in Sr2IrO4
paper.abstract_en: Correlated quantum phenomena arising from spin-orbit-coupled degrees of freedom provide foundational paradigms in emerging quantum technologies and spin-based functionalities. Elucidating the cooperative behaviors of these systems requires a precise probing of their intertwined magnetic and structural configurations. Using complementary resonant X-ray diffraction and high-energy total scattering measurements on single crystals of Sr2IrO4, we observe that spontaneous structural distortions scale quadratically with the magnetic order parameter. Importantly, the lattice distortion inherits the characteristic 2D XY -like critical behavior of the underlying antiferromagnetic order. X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) reveals multiscale, temperature- and wave-vector-dependent magnetic dynamics characterized by compressed-exponential relaxation and signatures of critical slowing down near the magnetic transition. These findings suggest the role of spin-orbit coupling and local structural distortions as the possible mechanism orchestrating such unconventional dynamics.
